layout_structure.layout_type: single column with title and flowchart
layout_structure.title_text: How do we get large-scale annotated data?
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a centered title at the top, enclosed within a light blue rounded rectangular box. The main body of the slide is occupied by a horizontal flowchart that details a data processing pipeline. On the far left, an unlabeled 3D snowman asset from Objaverse is shown. A blue arrow labeled 'multiview render' leads to two parallel rows of 2D snowman renders. These renders are overlaid with a grid of points, labeled 'gridpoint prompt', and then pass through green boxes labeled 'SAM'. The output of this stage is '2D masks', where specific parts of the snowman are highlighted in purple. These masks are then processed by yellow boxes labeled 'Gemini' with the instruction 'query part name'. A final arrow labeled 'unproject' leads to the rightmost section, which displays the resulting 3D annotated parts labeled with mathematical notation such as T(base) and T(snowball). A circular video inset of the presenter is located in the bottom right corner. The slide has a white background and moderate text density, primarily consisting of labels for the diagram's components.

layout_structure.layout_type: methodology diagram layout
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a large, bold title 'Method' positioned at the top-left. The main body of the slide is dominated by a horizontal flowchart-style diagram. On the left, two primary components are stacked: a grey box labeled 'inference' showing a 'Find3D transformer' processing a 3D snowman model, and a pink box labeled 'Data Engine'. These components feed into a contrastive learning framework on the right. This framework shows pairs of snowman images with specific parts highlighted (like the base or hat) being mapped to corresponding feature vectors, represented by yellow and pink vertical bars. These are labeled as 'positive pair' and grouped together by a large bracket at the bottom labeled 'Contrastive loss'. Below this diagram, there is a list of three key features, each marked with a green checkmark icon: 'Simple model, simple training recipe', 'Handles ambiguity', and 'Scalable'. A circular video feed of the presenter is visible in the bottom-right corner of the slide.
